In the water, sieve miso paste through a fine sieve
Add wakame seaweed, sliced tofu and green scallions

instructions: Start in the cold pan with beaten eggs and butter
Periodically take the pan on and off the heat constantly stirring until the eggs come out creamy and smooth

name: Sushi Rice
instructions: Rinse rice until clear
Let rice soak in water for 30 minutes
Add equal parts water and rice to rice cooker and place the kombu on top
Make the sushi ingest buy combining the rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan and bring to boil over medium high heat until sugar is dissolved, let cool
After the rice is cooked, while hot, evenly mix the rice seasoning mixture with the rice.

name: Dashi Stock
notes: Store in a jar and keep in fridge for 3-5 days or freezer for 2 weeks.
instructions: In a medium pot, add kombu and water.
On low medium heat, bring to bare simmer for 10 minutes
Right before it starts boiling, remove kombu from the pot
Add bonito flakes and bring to a boil
When boiling, reduce heat and simmer for 30 seconds then turn off the heat
Let bonito flakes simmer for 10 minutes
Strain the dashi

name: Chinese Tea Egg
notes: Can be stored for 4-5 days in the fridge
instructions: Add all marinade, tea, seasoning and water to a pot, bring to boil at medium low heat, simmer for 10 minutes, then let completely cool
Boil eggs for 5 minutes for soft boil then put in ice bath for 2-3 minutes
Gently crack eggs with back of the spoon
Put with marinade and marinate for 24 hours

Freeze

instructions: Defrost the mix, add the egg mix and pan fry

name: Soba Noodle Salad
description: Chilled soba noodles tossed in a sesame-soy-honey dressing with scallions and cilantro.
instructions: Warm the neutral oil, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes together over medium heat for about 3 minutes to infuse the oil.
Take the pan off the heat, let it cool slightly, then whisk in the honey until dissolved.
Whisk in the soy sauce to finish the dressing, then set it aside.
Boil the soba noodles until just shy of al dente, a little under the package time.
While the noodles cook, slice the green onions and roughly chop the cilantro.
Drain the noodles and rinse well under cold water to wash off the surface starch.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, green onions, cilantro, and sesame seeds.
Serve chilled or at room temperature.

name: Cold Udon (Zaru Udon)
description: Chilled udon served with a cold Memmi dipping sauce, scallions, and nori.
instructions: Mix the Memmi with cold water in a 1:4 ratio to make the dipping sauce, then chill it.
Boil the udon noodles according to package directions until tender.
Drain and rinse the noodles thoroughly under cold water, then chill.
Divide the noodles between bowls or arrange on a serving plate.
Top with sliced green onion and nori strips.
Serve with the chilled dipping sauce on the side for dipping.

name: Cold Soba (Zaru Soba)
description: Chilled soba served with a cold Memmi dipping sauce, scallions, and nori.
instructions: Mix the Memmi with cold water in a 1:4 ratio to make the dipping sauce, then chill it.
Boil the soba noodles until just tender, being careful not to overcook them.
Drain and rinse well under cold water to remove surface starch, then chill.
Divide the noodles between bowls or arrange on a serving plate.
Top with sliced green onion and nori strips.
Serve with the chilled dipping sauce on the side for dipping.

name: Yakisoba (Pork)
description: Japanese stir-fried noodles with pork belly, cabbage, and shiitake, tossed in yakisoba sauce.
instructions: Warm the yakisoba noodles on a hot pan with a little oil, gently loosening them apart.
Cook the pork belly until no longer pink, then add the onion and cook until softened.
Add the cabbage, shiitake mushrooms, and green onion, and stir-fry until everything is tender.
Return the noodles to the pan, pour the yakisoba sauce over everything, and toss until evenly coated.
Season with black pepper and plate immediately.

name: Bok Choy and Tofu Stir-Fry
description: A quick stir-fry of deep-fried tofu, bok choy, and shimeji mushrooms in a light savory sauce.
instructions: Slice the bok choy, separating the stems from the leafy greens, cut the tofu into cubes, and mince the ginger and garlic.
Heat the sesame oil over medium heat and sauté the ginger and garlic until fragrant.
Add the tofu and bok choy stems, stirring until the tofu browns and the stems begin to soften; season with salt and pepper.
Add the bok choy leaves and mushrooms, and cook until the greens wilt and the mushrooms are tender.
Whisk the vegetable stock base, water, soy sauce, and corn starch together, pour into the pan, and stir constantly until the sauce thickens. Serve immediately.

name: Beef Udon (Niku Udon)
description: Udon noodles in a warm dashi broth, topped with soy-glazed sliced beef and green onion.
instructions: Warm the dashi and season it with soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and salt; keep it warm.
Slice the green onion diagonally.
Sauté the green onion in oil until golden, then add the sliced beef.
Season the beef with sugar and soy sauce and cook until glazed.
Cook the udon noodles according to the package directions and drain.
Divide the noodles between bowls, ladle the hot broth over them, and top with the beef and green onion. Sprinkle with togarashi if desired.

name: Soboro Udon
description: Udon noodles topped with sweet-savory ground chicken and a soft poached egg.
instructions: Slice the green onion diagonally, keeping the white and green parts separate, and grate the ginger; stir the mirin, soy sauce, sugar, and corn starch together in a small bowl.
Heat the sesame oil and sauté the white parts of the green onion with the ginger until fragrant, then add the ground chicken and cook until no longer pink.
Pour in the sauce mixture and simmer until it thickens to your liking.
Poach or soft-boil the eggs so the whites are set but the yolks stay runny.
Reheat the udon noodles in boiling water, then divide between bowls and top with the chicken sauce.
Place a poached egg on top of each bowl and garnish with the green onion tops and togarashi.

name: Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
description: Double-fried Japanese fried chicken thighs, marinated in ginger, garlic, soy sauce, and sake.
instructions: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sake, and sesame oil in a bowl, add the chicken, and marinate for about 30 minutes.
Heat frying oil to around 325°F (160°C) in a deep pot (not tracked as a pantry ingredient — most of it is strained and reused, not consumed).
Coat each piece of chicken first in flour, then in cornstarch, shaking off the excess.
Fry the chicken in small batches for about 90 seconds until lightly golden, then drain on a wire rack.
Raise the oil temperature to about 350°F (180°C) and fry each piece again briefly until crispy and deep golden brown.
Serve hot, with lemon wedges or other garnishes on the side if you like.

name: Udon Noodle Soup (Kake Udon)
description: Simple udon noodles in a warm soy-dashi broth, topped with green onion.
instructions: Combine the dashi, mirin, sugar, soy sauce, and salt in a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer; cover and keep warm.
Boil a separate pot of water and cook the udon noodles per the package instructions, stirring to loosen them.
Drain the noodles and divide them between bowls.
Pour the hot broth over the noodles and top with sliced green onion and togarashi if desired.

name: Gyudon (Japanese Beef Rice Bowl)
description: Thinly sliced beef and onion simmered in a sweet soy sauce, served over rice.
instructions: Slice the onion thinly and cut the semi-frozen beef into thin strips.
Combine the dashi, sake, mirin, soy sauce, and sugar in a cold frying pan, without heat.
Layer the sliced onion, then the beef, over the sauce.
Cover and bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce the heat and cook covered for 3-4 minutes, skimming off any foam.
Add the green onion, cook covered for another minute, then serve the beef and onion mixture over the rice, spooning the sauce on top.

name: Oyakodon (Chicken and Egg Bowl)
description: Quick chicken and egg simmered in a sweet soy dashi broth, served over rice.
instructions: Slice the onion, cut the green onion diagonally (keeping white and green parts separate), cube the chicken into bite-sized pieces, and lightly beat the eggs.
Combine the water, dashi powder, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, onion, and the white parts of the green onion in a small pan.
Arrange the chicken on top, cover, and cook over high heat for about 3 minutes.
Flip the chicken and cook uncovered for another 1-2 minutes until no longer pink.
Lower the heat, drizzle the beaten eggs over the chicken along with the green onion tops, and cook until the eggs are just set.
Serve over the steamed rice, with togarashi on top if desired.

name: Tanindon (Beef and Egg Rice Bowl)
description: Thinly sliced beef and onion simmered in a sweet soy sauce, finished with softly set egg over rice.
instructions: Slice the onion thinly, cut the green onion into strips, and beat the eggs in a bowl.
Combine the dashi, soy sauce, sake, mirin, and sugar in a large frying pan.
Spread the onion in the pan, then layer the beef on top.
Cover and cook over medium heat until the beef is cooked through, skimming off any foam.
Reduce the heat and simmer, covered, for 3-4 minutes.
Slowly drizzle the beaten eggs over the beef without stirring, add the green onion, and cook covered until the eggs reach your preferred doneness.
Divide the rice between bowls, top with the beef and egg mixture, and sprinkle with togarashi if desired.

name: Sous Vide Filet Mignon Prep
description: Seasoned filet mignon vacuum sealed with butter and rosemary, ready to sous vide.
instructions: Season the filet mignon generously with salt and pepper.
Place the steak in a vacuum seal bag with the butter and rosemary.
Vacuum seal the bag and refrigerate or freeze until ready to cook.

name: Sous Vide Seared Filet Mignon
description: Sous vide filet mignon finished with a hard sear in beef tallow.
instructions: Sous vide the bagged steak at 130°F (54°C) for 45-50 minutes.
Remove the steak from the bag and pat it dry.
Heat the beef tallow in a cast iron skillet over high heat.
Sear the steak for about 1 minute per side until a deep crust forms, then rest briefly before serving.

name: Pan-Fried Salmon Fillet
description: A quick, simple Japanese-style pan-seared salmon fillet with just salt and pepper.
instructions: Pat the salmon fillet dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Pan-fry the salmon, skin-side down first if it has skin, until golden and cooked through, flipping once.

name: Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: Blanched broccoli stir-fried with garlic in a savory oyster sauce glaze.
instructions: Cut the broccoli into florets and slice the stems; mince the garlic.
Stir together the sauce ingredients (salt, sugar, cooking wine, chicken bouillon, cornstarch, water, and oyster sauce) in a bowl and set aside.
Blanch the broccoli in salted, oiled boiling water for about 3 minutes, then shock it in an ice bath.
Stir-fry the garlic in oil until fragrant, add the broccoli and a splash of cooking wine, then pour in the sauce and toss until glossy and coated.

name: Scrambled Eggs with Chives
description: Soft scrambled eggs stir-fried with chives, lightly seasoned and thickened with a potato starch slurry.
instructions: Soak, rinse, and cut the chives into ¾-inch pieces.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add the seasonings and the potato starch slurry (starch mixed with water), and beat until bubbly.
Heat a wok with a little oil, stir-fry the chives until fragrant, then mix them into the beaten eggs.
Wipe out the wok, reheat with the remaining oil, pour in the egg mixture, stir briefly, flip, and cook until just set.
Drizzle a bit more oil around the edge of the wok and transfer to a plate immediately.

name: Universal Stir Fry Sauce
description: A make-ahead all-purpose stir-fry sauce base to keep on hand.
instructions: Boil ¼ cup of water.
Combine the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, salt, chicken bouillon, and the hot water in a bowl and mix thoroughly.
Refrigerate the sauce in a sealed container until ready to use.
To use, measure out about a third to a quarter of the batch per stir-fry, thickening with a cornstarch slurry near the end of cooking if desired.

name: Chinese Smashed Cucumber Salad
description: Smashed cucumbers tossed in a garlicky chili oil and vinegar dressing.
instructions: Halve the cucumbers lengthwise, then smash them with the flat of a knife blade until they split.
Slice the cucumbers diagonally into ½-inch pieces.
Sprinkle the salt over the cucumbers and let them sit for about 20 minutes, then drain off the excess liquid.
Mix the grated garlic with the rice vinegar and let it sit for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, chili oil, sugar, and sesame oil.
Toss the cucumbers with the sauce just before serving, and garnish with sesame seeds.

name: Choy Sum with Garlic
description: Choy sum stems and leaves quickly steamed and stir-fried with garlic and ginger.
instructions: Separate the choy sum leaves from the stems, cutting them at an angle.
Slice some of the garlic and mince the rest; thinly slice the ginger.
Heat the wok with oil over medium-low heat, then stir-fry the ginger and garlic for about 15 seconds.
Add the stems first and cook for 30 seconds, then add the leaves, raise the heat, and add the cooking wine and sugar, stir-frying for 30 seconds.
Cover and steam for 1.5-2 minutes over medium-low heat until tender, then uncover, raise the heat, add the salt, and toss for another 20 seconds before serving.

name: Dried Scallop and Egg White Fried Rice
description: Jasmine rice fried with rehydrated dried scallops, silky egg whites, ginger, and green onion.
instructions: Rinse the rice three times and cook it in a rice cooker with the water; soak the dried scallops in hot water until softened, about 20 minutes or more.
Chop the green onions into small pieces and finely mince the ginger.
Separate the egg whites from the yolks; shred the softened scallops; fluff the cooked rice once done.
Cook the egg whites in a hot, oiled wok until just set, then set aside; fry half the shredded scallops until golden and reserve them separately.

Stir-fry the ginger with the remaining scallops, add the rice, season with salt, sugar, and fish sauce, fold in the egg whites, finish with sesame oil and green onions, and top with the fried scallops.

name: Shrimp and Snow Pea Stir-Fry
description: Marinated shrimp stir-fried with snow peas, celery, carrot, and mushroom in a savory sauce.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, then marinate with white pepper, salt, and cornstarch.
String the snow peas, cut the celery into strips, and slice the carrot into diamond shapes.
Slice the ginger and green onion, mince the garlic, and trim the mushroom ends.
Stir together the sauce ingredients in a bowl.
Blanch the celery and carrot first, then the snow peas, then the mushrooms, in salted boiling water.
Heat the wok and stir-fry the shrimp until just white, then transfer to a plate.
Stir-fry the aromatics, add the vegetables and shrimp back in, season with the wine and sauce, and finish with a touch of sesame oil.

name: Cantonese Scrambled Eggs with Shrimp
description: Silky Cantonese-style scrambled eggs folded with lightly marinated shrimp.
instructions: Peel, devein, and thoroughly pat dry the shrimp, then marinate with salt, white pepper, and cornstarch.
Chop the green onion; beat the eggs with oil, salt, and sugar until fluffy, stirring in the green onion just before cooking.
Heat the wok on high and stir-fry the shrimp briefly until mostly cooked, then transfer into the egg mixture.
Add the remaining oil to the wok, pour in the combined egg and shrimp mixture, and fold continuously as it cooks to your desired doneness.
Transfer to a plate immediately to keep the eggs from overcooking.

name: Stir Fried Bok Choy
description: Quick stir-fried baby bok choy with garlic, lightly seasoned.
instructions: Rinse the bok choy thoroughly, separating the stems and scrubbing any dirt from the base.
Drain and pat the bok choy dry, then trim the stems lengthwise.
Heat the wok on high for 2-3 minutes while mincing the garlic, then add the oil until shimmering.
Briefly cook the garlic, then add the bok choy stalks and leaves, stir-frying for 6-8 minutes until tender.
Season with salt, sugar, and chicken bouillon just before serving, and plate immediately.

name: Egg Drop Soup
description: Silky egg-ribboned soup with peas, corn, and carrots.
instructions: Dice the green onions and carrots into small pieces.
Bring the water to a boil in a covered pot.
Whisk the eggs with a little water in a bowl.
Add the carrots, corn, and peas to the boiling water.
Mix the cornstarch with water until smooth to make a slurry, then stir it gradually into the soup over about 30 seconds.
Slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs while stirring constantly for about 20 seconds.
Turn off the heat and season with salt, chicken bouillon, white pepper, and sesame oil.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh green onion.

name: Chicken Corn Soup
description: A silky corn puree soup with marinated diced chicken, egg ribbons, and cilantro.
instructions: Dice the chicken breast and marinate it with cornstarch, salt, and water until absorbed.
Blend the corn with water into a smooth puree; dice the carrot into small cubes.
Mix the cornstarch slurry in a small bowl and beat the egg in a separate bowl.
Bring water to a boil, add the corn puree and carrot, then slowly stir in the slurry, chicken, and egg while stirring constantly.
Season with salt, chicken powder, white pepper, and sesame oil, then garnish with cilantro and serve.

name: Bok Choy in Chicken Broth
description: Bok choy simmered in a simple chicken bouillon broth, served as vegetables in broth.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil and stir in the chicken bouillon to make a broth.
Add the bok choy and simmer until just tender.
Ladle the bok choy and broth into a bowl and serve.

name: Choy Sum in Chicken Broth
description: Choy sum simmered in a simple chicken bouillon broth, served as vegetables in broth.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil and stir in the chicken bouillon to make a broth.
Add the choy sum and simmer until just tender.
Ladle the choy sum and broth into a bowl and serve.
